evaluations.label: A
errors: Building named 'UniMile'; the transcript says Unimail.
'Susan and Martin both raised concerns about sharing offices': Martin said he has nothing against sharing and did it before; his only point was that his roommate must tolerate phone calls.
'The group discussed meeting the following Tuesday afternoon, around 2 p.m.': this was agreed, not just discussed, and it is omitted from the action items.
'There are 15 people and about 18 office positions, including part-time staff': the 18 are positions in the offices, not people; wording muddles the two counts.
strengths: Nearly every claim checks out against the transcript, with correct speaker names (Martin for growth-will-be-zero, Susan for the room-split idea and the rectorate confidentiality point, Susan volunteering to ask Maggie and Pierrette).
Clear structure: summary, then rooms, sharing, grouping/lounge, next steps; readable in a minute.
Correctly states the fixed/not-fixed split (room count fixed, assignments open) and that no layout was decided.
Captures the Gisella placement options and that the second seat in a two-person room is unresolved.
weaknesses: Action items list only two of the follow-ups; missing Andre checking whether four desks fit in a 3P room, Andre asking whether Gisella can sit with the school's other admin, and every attendee bringing a sketch/proposal to next Tuesday 2pm.
Omits David's stated preference to share with an assistant and to keep his own desk.
Omits the other group's role (Andre and Agnes will negotiate with them) and the coffee/cafeteria facts.
Next meeting time is buried in the body rather than stated as a decision.

evaluations.label: B
errors: Action item 'Follow up with absent team members (Maggie, Pierrette)' assigned to Andrei; Susan volunteered to do this ('Okay, I'll ask Maggie and Pierrette').
Action item 'Distribute documents of the new office configuration to all participants': Andre handed out the copies during the meeting; this is not an open task.

'Management recognizes this [the lounge] as a priority due to previously lengthy discussions on its value': unsupported; Martin's remark about the time spent discussing the room was a joke to Susan, and Susan questioned whether the lounge is needed at all.
'Smoking is allowed only outside, even on balconies' reads as if balconies are off limits; Susan said you can go out onto the balcony to smoke.
'Growth is effectively zero unless visitors or temporary staff share existing desks': the sharing clause is invented; the group explicitly rejected sharing desks.
'The session [next Tuesday] will focus on refining the plan rather than final decisions': Andre said the next meeting is to come with one solution.
'merge proposals with another group before next Tuesday's review meeting': Andre said the merge happens when the other group's proposal is available, not before Tuesday.
'Splitting rooms ... currently not feasible due to building and security regulations' stated as settled; Andre said the answer is probably no for now but he will find out.
'The team expects to manage this through proposals and iterative feedback rather than direct surveys': Andre asked everyone to poll colleagues directly; Martin's point was an aside.
Building named 'Unimile'; the transcript says Unimail.
strengths: Most complete coverage of topics: four desks in a 3P room, Gisella with the school's admin, room splitting authorisation, coffee machines and cafeteria hours, whiteboards and equipment, the other group's parallel proposal.
Correctly identifies the three investigations Andre took on and the all-participants proposal task.
Next meeting captured as Tuesday afternoon around 14:00 with the reason (morning conflict).
weaknesses: Far too long and padded with generic management-speak ('Open dialogue is encouraged', 'Coordination ... is critical to ensure inclusive planning') that is not in the transcript; the same points repeat across four or five sections.
Two of seven action items are wrong (wrong owner for Maggie/Pierrette; a bogus 'distribute documents' task), which undercuts trust in the list.
Almost no speaker attribution: a reader cannot tell who wants a private office, who objects to project grouping, or who will ask the absent professors.
Several embellishments presented as fact (management priority, iterative-feedback process, next session 'not final').

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'Majority lean toward a mixed-use room': Martin said he belongs to the people wanting a mixed room and that no final decision has been taken; no majority was established.
'Strong support for a dedicated lounge/reading room': Andre said quite a lot of people expressed the need, but Susan asked 'Do we really need that?'; 'strong' overstates it.
Building spelled 'Unimile' in the overview but 'Unimail' (correct) under next steps.
'give her a 2P room with a visitor slot' omits that Martin called that unrealistic for a senior visitor (only an exchange student or intern).
strengths: Tight and accurate: correct counts (15 people, ~18 positions, 16 if a 2P room becomes the reading room, zero growth margin), correct furniture list, correct smoking and coffee facts.

Next steps are the most complete of the four: room separation, four desks in a 3P room, Gisella with the school admin, Maggie/Pierrette preferences, everyone brings a sketch, Tuesday 2pm after the MDM meeting at Unimail.
Correctly reports that project grouping was rejected and why, that each person keeps their own desk, and that the room split is ruled out for now pending confirmation.
Correctly notes Andre and Agnes will negotiate with the other group (David's line) and that lounge furnishing is deferred.
weaknesses: Next steps carry no owners; a reader would not know Andre owns the three investigations and Susan owns Maggie/Pierrette.
Omits David's preference to share with an assistant for day-to-day problems, and that only one slot is fully free today (one visitor at a time).
Omits Martin's point that attendees can only speak for themselves, and the suggestion to ask people only for their own place.
Some claims read as more settled than the transcript supports (majority view on the lounge).

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'to accommodate approximately 15 to 18 people': there are 15 people and about 18 positions, not 15 to 18 people.

'Action Items: (none)': Andre will check room separation and four desks in a 3P room and whether Gisella can sit with the school admin; Susan will ask Maggie and Pierrette; everyone brings a proposal for Tuesday 2pm.

'professors should share offices with their assistants, noting this is common in other faculties but not necessarily here': reversed. Andre said sharing with assistants is an implicit tradition at this school; Susan said every other faculty gives professors their own office.
'There is uncertainty regarding whether grouping should be based on specific projects': Martin said no to project grouping, Susan agreed, and Andre confirmed nobody felt attached to it.

Speakers labelled 'Speaker 1/2/3/4' with no mapping to the names used in the meeting (Andre, Susan, Martin, David), so 'Speaker 1 noted ... confidential discussions regarding budgets' cannot be checked and actually merges Susan's rectorate point with Martin's budget point.
'Members were tasked with consulting colleagues, such as Maggie and Pierrette': Susan volunteered for Maggie and Pierrette specifically; the others were asked to poll people around them.
strengths: Unresolved-questions list is a fair summary of the open items (room partitions, four in a 3P room, lounge purpose, professors' preference for individual offices).
Next meeting Tuesday 2:00 PM is correct.
Core space facts (room sizes, furniture, equipment, part-time Martin and David, another group proposing) are right.
weaknesses: Empty action-item section while the outline itself names follow-ups; a reader would conclude nothing was assigned.
Numbered speaker labels make attribution useless for someone who missed the meeting.
Misses Gisella-with-school-admin option, the one-free-slot point, smoking, coffee, and that the other group's proposal will be merged by Andre and Agnes.
Summary and outline duplicate each other with little added detail.

rationale: C is the best balance: accurate numbers and attributions, the most complete next-steps list (all three of Andre's checks, Susan's poll of Maggie and Pierrette, everyone's sketch, Tuesday 2pm), and short enough to act on; its gaps are missing owners and a slightly overstated lounge consensus. A is nearly as accurate and reads well, but its action list drops three of the five follow-ups and the meeting time, so a reader would under-act. B covers the most ground but pays for it with padding, invented framing (management priority, iterative-feedback process), and two wrong action items including the wrong owner for the Maggie/Pierrette poll. D says there are no action items when there were several, reverses the professor-sharing tradition, miscounts people as '15 to 18', and uses unmapped speaker numbers, so it is least trustworthy and least usable.
